relationships.description: The view gathers one or more independently persisted base collections into a single readable result set, and those collections continue to exist and accept writes whether or not the view is defined.
relationships.evidence: The view's DDL or pipeline definition (e.g. CREATE VIEW ... FROM orders JOIN customers, or a MongoDB $lookup/$unionWith) names the collections it combines.

relationships.description: The view exposes a projection of stored fields drawn from its source collections as its own output columns, while those fields remain owned by and persisted in the underlying collections.
relationships.evidence: The view's SELECT list, $project stage or alias definition explicitly lists the source columns or document paths it surfaces.

relationships.description: The index is a lookup structure built over the view's precomputed contents (typically a materialized or indexed view) and is dropped when the view is dropped.
relationships.evidence: A CREATE INDEX statement targets the materialized view by name, or the engine catalog (e.g. pg_indexes, sys.indexes) lists the index with the view as its parent object.

relationships.description: The view's contents are computed by its stored query or pipeline from the records held in the base collection, so changes to that collection change what the view returns.
relationships.evidence: The view definition in the schema migration or engine catalog references the base table or collection in its FROM clause, pipeline source or alias target.

relationships.description: The view is layered on another view, computing its contents from that upstream view's derived result rather than directly from base collections.
relationships.evidence: The view's definition query selects from another view by name, and the engine's dependency catalog (e.g. pg_depend, information_schema.view_table_usage) records the view-on-view dependency.

relationships.description: The view supplies the exact data shape that an API operation returns, so the response body schema is a direct serialization of the view's rows or documents.
relationships.evidence: The handler for the operation reads from the view and returns its rows, and the OpenAPI response schema properties match the view's projected columns one-to-one.

relationships.description: The view provides a ready-made read model that the application service queries to fulfil its operations, such as reporting, search or dashboard lookups.
relationships.evidence: The application service's repository or data-access code issues queries against the view name, or the ORM maps a read-only entity to the view.

relationships.description: The view furnishes the curated, derived data that a business service relies on to deliver its outcome, such as a consolidated customer or reporting dataset used by analysts.
relationships.evidence: Business service documentation or a data catalog entry identifies the view as the authoritative dataset for that service, and BI reports or extracts supporting the service query it.

notes: aggregates→collection largely duplicates derives-from→collection; derives-from is the accurate semantics. aggregates→field is odd since fields belong to persisted collections, not views. realizes→api.response and serves→businessservice skip intermediate application/API layers and are weak; serves→applicationservice is the more defensible link.
